newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta Safeway employees to strike.
newsitem.headline: Alberta Safeway employees to strike.

text.p: Unionized employees at Canada Safeway Ltd's 73 grocery stores in Alberta plan to go on strike at midnight on Tuesday, a week before voting on a final labor offer from the company, unions and management said.
The final offer from Canada Safeway, a unit of Pleasonton, California-based Safeway Inc and Alberta's largest grocery chain, was presented to the unions on Monday after talks broke down.
The company's clerks, meat cutters and bakers in Alberta stores voted overwhelmingly in favor of a strike last week.

Officials with the United Food and Commercial Workers union said they would urge members to reject the last-minute deal when employees in Edmonton and Calgary vote on it Monday and Tuesday. A schedule for voting in other cities had yet to be determined.
The company, which has 10,000 employees in the western Canadian province, offered a 50-cent per hour wage hike and C$1,000 lump-sum payment for full-time staff if the deal was ratified.
The five-year deal would also give full-time and senior part-time employees pay hikes of 30 cents an hour in 1998 and 40 cents in 2000.
Canada Safeway said the offer was worth an increase of C$2 an hour for those employees earning more than C$14 an hour. Those currently taking home less would get an increase of C$1.17.
The final deal did not fully restore C$2 an hour wage rollbacks the company's employees took in 1993. Union negotiators had demanded during the talks that the pay be made up.
"We find the union's position extremely unfortunate," Canada Safeway president Grant Hansen said.

"Why would the union leaders subject our employees to a loss of wages and benefits, and risk a loss of sales that would further impact our employees, before they have had an opportunity to vote on the offer?"
Hansen, in a letter to union leaders, on Tuesday proposed lifting the two sides' strike and lockout notices.
Meanwhile, the company has trained about 2,000 replacement workers so it could continue operations during the strike.

Canada Safeway's big competitors in Alberta, Loblaw Cos Ltd unit The Real Canadian Superstore and Co-op stores, a member cooperative, have served notice they planned to woo Safeway customers in the event of a labor disruption.
